simple.meaning: נָתִיב (nâthîyb) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a (beaten) track.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 26 times across Judges, Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, and 3 more, beginning at Judges 5:6. Its contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָתִיב (H5410).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָתִיב (nâthîyb) / H5410 is traced through Judges 5:6, Job 18:10, Job 19:8, Job 24:13 as a generated source-based concept entry.

occurrences.englishText: “In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath,
A noose is hidden for him in the ground,
He has walled up my way so that I can’t pass,
“These are of those who rebel against the light.
That path no bird of prey knows,
They mar my path.
that you should take it to its bound,
His heart is as firm as a stone,
He made a path for his anger.
Direct me in the path of your commandments,
Your word is a lamp to my feet,
Look on my right, and see;
My son, don’t walk on the path with them.
Her ways are ways of pleasantness.
Don’t let your heart turn to her ways.
On the top of high places by the way,
I walk in the way of righteousness,
In the way of righteousness is life;
I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know.
Yahweh, who makes a way in the sea,
Those who will be of you will build the old waste places.
They don’t know the way of peace;
Yahweh says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it.’
For my people have forgotten me.
He has walled up my ways with cut stone.
For she didn’t know that I gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil,
